title: Digital twins
none: You may not see any digital twin yet. Ask an administrator for access (the group twin:<id>).
noneAdmin: There is no digital twin yet.
idHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; it can't change later. Its viewers are the group twin:<id>.
access: Who sees it: administrators and the members of the group {{group}} in the identity provider.
name: Name
confirmDelete: Delete the twin {{name}} with its dashboards and saved filters? Its history stays until it expires.

secret.keep: Kept as it is; type to replace it

kubernetes.connection: The cluster this service runs in (its read-only account), or any other through a kubeconfig.
kubernetes.kubeconfig: Its user must sign in with a token (kubectl create token <account> --duration 0) and everything must be inline: certificate-authority-data, no files.
kubernetes.clusterName: The root twin's label; empty: the twin's id.
kubernetes.cephManagers: The Ceph managers' Prometheus pages (http://host:9283/metrics), comma-separated: pools and disks in the twin.
kubernetes.externalDisks: How the nodes' disks other than the internal NVMe/eMMC (Ceph's sdX) are attached: drawn as USB disks on USB ports, or as internal SATA disks.
kubernetes.lan: Nodes wired to one switch, the switch to the router in front of the internet: both in the twin with their ports and cables.
kubernetes.switchModel: Shown in the switch's detail; empty: unknown.
kubernetes.routerModel: Shown in the router's detail; empty: unknown.
kubernetes.clickhouseUrl: Where the cluster's OpenTelemetry Collector writes logs, metrics and traces; empty: this service's own ClickHouse.
kubernetes.clickhouseCluster: The k8s.cluster.name the collector stamps the telemetry with; empty: everything in that ClickHouse.
kubernetes.lanDevices: One per line as kind:name or kind:model:name (kind: ap, switch, router): each cabled to a free port of the switch; an access point (ap) also gets its Wi-Fi port.
kubernetes.externalServices: URLs probed at every sync, comma-separated: twins on the internet's globe with their status (e.g. https://api.mistral.ai for the agent's Mistral).

connection.inCluster: The cluster this service runs in

data.profileHelp: The twin runs one data profile at a time: its models' dataProfiles say where each profile's telemetry comes from (live data, a simulation, a replay).
data.connectionsHelp: Where the profiles' bindings read, by id. Addresses and credentials live here, never in the models; secrets are write-only.
data.idHelp: Short id the models' bindings name (a-z, 0-9, -).

typeHelp.clickhouse: A SELECT per twin; the twin's values go in as typed parameters. Use a read-only user.
typeHelp.prometheus: An instant PromQL query per twin (Prometheus, Mimir, VictoriaMetrics, Thanos…).
typeHelp.mqtt: A topic per twin; the value at a path in each message.
typeHelp.kafka: A topic; each message matched to its twin by its key or a field.
typeHelp.rabbitmq: An own queue bound to an exchange by a routing key per twin.
typeHelp.generator: Values from a pattern over time, for simulations. Reaches nothing.
typeHelp.kubernetes-simulation: The simulation's own cluster (kwok, kind…), named by a simulation profile's simulator.

assets.title: 3D models
assets.help: Binary glTF files (.glb) that hold everything themselves — no files outside them, no Draco or meshopt compression. A model's drawing places one by its name: { "shape": "gltf", "asset": "<name>" } in presentation.visual.parts. The built-in ones (a mini PC, a router, a switch, a USB disk) are drawn by the presets; uploading one of the same name replaces it in this twin.
assets.name: Name
assets.confirmDelete: Delete the 3D model {{name}}? Drawings that place it show nothing in its place.
